title: Painful red right eye after a night at the cinema
disclaimer: Fictional case written for the Eye Academy developer take-home. Not a real patient.
opening_prompt: A 64-year-old woman attends eye casualty at 23:40 with a painful red right eye. Ask me for any examination findings you need, then tell me your diagnosis and immediate management.

patient.presenting_complaint: Sudden severe pain in the right eye with blurred vision, haloes around lights, frontal headache, nausea and one episode of vomiting. Started about 3 hours ago while watching a film in a dark cinema.
patient.past_ocular_history: Long-sighted, wears reading and distance glasses. No previous eye surgery or laser.
medications: Chlorphenamine 4 mg (over the counter), started 2 days ago for hay fever

findings.label: Conjunctiva
findings.value: Diffuse injection, most marked around the limbus (ciliary flush)

findings.label: Anterior chamber depth
findings.value: Shallow, Van Herick grade 1 (peripheral depth under 1/4 of corneal thickness)

findings.label: Relative afferent pupillary defect
findings.unavailable_reason: Right pupil fixed, so the test cannot be interpreted

findings.label: Gonioscopy
findings.value: Iridotrabecular contact in 3 of 4 quadrants, no peripheral anterior synechiae on indentation

findings.label: Optic disc and fundus
findings.value: Healthy disc, cup-to-disc ratio 0.3, normal macula

findings.label: Refraction
findings.value: Right +3.50 DS, left +3.25 DS (from her current glasses)

examiner_notes.diagnosis: Right acute primary angle closure, with a narrow left angle at risk. Likely triggered by dim light and a new anticholinergic antihistamine.
key_points: Lower the pressure: topical agents (e.g. beta-blocker, alpha-agonist, pilocarpine once the pressure starts to fall), plus systemic treatment as appropriate
Note the sulfonamide allergy before giving acetazolamide
Laser peripheral iridotomy to both eyes once the cornea clears, including the fellow eye
Review gonioscopy of the right eye and the optic discs after the attack settles
follow_up_ideas: Why treat the left eye as well?
Why might pilocarpine not work at first when the pressure is very high?
What would you do if the pressure doesn't come down?

reference_source.title: Glaucoma and angle closure: Eye Academy reference note
reference_source.note: Cite by page number. The acute primary angle closure section is the main source; the other sections act as distractors.
